title: How to diagnose and fix stalled growth: Jason Cohen's five-question checklist
summary: Jason Cohen walks through an ordered diagnostic for stalled SaaS growth: logo churn, pricing and positioning, net revenue retention, channel saturation, and whether you need to grow at all. Includes the churn-cap formula, the Double Down 8x pricing story, and why A/B testing mostly yields false positives.

principles.text: Churn caps your size: max customers = new customers per month divided by monthly cancellation rate.
principles.quote: it's simply the amount of new customers you add divided by that cancellation rate. That is the amount that that is the limit.

principles.text: Cancellations grow automatically with your base while marketing output stays flat, so churn always overtakes acquisition.
principles.quote: cancellations grow faster than marketing and so cancellations overpower the growth of the company and slow it to a halt

principles.text: Ask 'what made you cancel?' not 'why', and never accept 'too expensive' as the real reason.
principles.quote: The wrong way is to ask why did you cancel?

principles.text: Early-stage prices are usually too low; raising them often leaves signups flat because pricing selects the market.
principles.quote: What often happens is you raise prices and signups don't change.

principles.text: Position around what the buyer values (growth) rather than savings to unlock a far higher price ceiling.
principles.quote: sell more of what the company values like growth.

principles.text: Channels saturate and then sag, so don't just push marketing harder or add a feature.
principles.quote: Do you know right now which channels are saturated and which aren't?
